examples.ko: 아이들 학원비가 요즘 제일 큰 두통거리예요.
examples.en: My kids' tuition is the biggest headache for me these days.

examples.ko: 이사 날짜가 안 정해져서 두통거리가 하나 더 생겼어요.
examples.en: The moving date isn't set, so I have one more headache.
That problem is probably a headache for the company too.

examples.ko: 주차 문제가 동네 사람들에게 두통거리가 됐어요.
examples.en: Parking has become a headache for the people in the neighborhood.
For me, the presentation was more of a headache than the homework.
If you sort out your worries one by one, you feel at ease.

explain: '골칫거리'와 거의 같은 말이에요. 사람이든 일이든 '속을 썩이는 대상'에 쓰고, '두통거리가 되다/생기다'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: It is almost the same as '골칫거리'. It is used for a person or a thing that causes you trouble, as in '두통거리가 되다/생기다'.

examples.en: Every weekend I walk along the path on the riverbank.
Cherry blossoms are in full bloom on both sides of the embankment path.
It rained, so the embankment path is very slippery.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 이 둑길로 학교에 다녔어요.
examples.en: When I was little, I went to school along this embankment path.

examples.ko: 저녁에 둑길에서 자전거를 타는 사람이 많아요.
examples.en: In the evening, many people ride bikes on the embankment path.

examples.ko: 둑길이 끝나는 곳에 작은 다리가 하나 있어요.
examples.en: There is a small bridge where the embankment path ends.

explain: '둑'은 물을 막으려고 쌓은 언덕이고, '둑길'은 그 위나 옆으로 난 길이에요. 강이나 저수지 옆 산책길, 시골 풍경을 이야기할 때 자주 나와요.
explain_en: '둑' is a bank built to hold back water, and '둑길' is the path on top of it or beside it. It often comes up when talking about walking paths by rivers or reservoirs and about the countryside.

examples.ko: 저는 냄새에 둔감해서 잘 못 맡아요.
examples.en: I'm not sensitive to smells, so I can't smell well.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 남의 기분에 너무 둔감해요.
examples.en: He is too insensitive to other people's feelings.

examples.ko: 추위에 둔감한 편이라 겨울에도 얇게 입어요.
examples.en: I don't really feel the cold, so I dress lightly even in winter.

examples.ko: 변화에 둔감하면 일하기 힘들어질 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you're slow to notice change, work can become hard.
They say you become less sensitive to taste as you get older.
I don't know why I was so oblivious to the mood.

explain: 반대말은 '민감하다'이고, 보통 '~에 둔감하다'처럼 '에'와 같이 써요. 말할 때는 '눈치가 없다', '무디다'라고도 해요.
explain_en: Its opposite is '민감하다', and it is usually used as '~에 둔감하다' with the particle '에'. In speech people also say '눈치가 없다' or '무디다'.

examples.en: The kids are running around on the grassy mound.

examples.ko: 집 뒤에 작은 둔덕이 하나 있어요.
examples.en: There is a small mound behind the house.
If you cross the mound, you can see the sea.
My bike caught on the mound and I almost fell.
We sat on the mound and ate our lunch boxes.
Because of the rain, the soil on the mound washed down.

explain: '언덕'보다 작고 낮게 솟은 곳을 말할 때 어울려요. 일상 대화에서는 그냥 '작은 언덕'이라고도 많이 말해요.
explain_en: It fits a spot that rises smaller and lower than a '언덕' (hill). In everyday talk people also often just say '작은 언덕' (a small hill).

examples.en: On the weekend I rode a bike on the Han River bank.

examples.ko: 비가 많이 오면 둔치 주차장이 물에 잠겨요.
examples.en: When it rains a lot, the riverside parking lot gets flooded.
We spread a mat on the riverside and ate fried chicken.
Every evening I run along the riverside.

examples.ko: 강 둔치에는 운동 시설이 잘 되어 있어요.
examples.en: The riverside has good exercise facilities.
Access to the riverside was blocked because of the flood.

explain: '강가'와 비슷하지만, 물가 옆에 평평하게 만들어 놓은 공원이나 운동 공간을 가리킬 때가 많아요. '한강 둔치'처럼 강 이름과 같이 자주 써요.
explain_en: It is similar to '강가' (riverside), but it often points to the flat park or exercise area made beside the water. It is often used with a river name, as in '한강 둔치'.

examples.en: The sound of knocking on the door is a bit dull.

examples.ko: 무거운 가방이 바닥에 떨어지는 둔탁한 소리가 났어요.
examples.en: There was a dull thud of a heavy bag falling on the floor.

examples.ko: 이불 때문에 소리가 둔탁하게 들렸나 봐요.
examples.en: The sound probably came across muffled because of the blanket.
When I tapped the wall, it gave a dull sound.

examples.ko: 위층에서 둔탁한 쿵 소리가 계속 들려요.
examples.en: I keep hearing a dull thump from upstairs.

examples.ko: 문이 닫히는 소리가 둔탁해서 깜짝 놀랐어요.
examples.en: The door closed with a heavy thud, and it startled me.

explain: '쿵', '퍽' 같은 무겁고 맑지 않은 소리를 말할 때 잘 어울려요. 반대로 맑고 높은 소리는 '맑다', '또렷하다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It suits heavy, unclear sounds like '쿵' or '퍽'. For clear, high sounds, people say '맑다' or '또렷하다' instead.

examples.en: It was cold, so I wrapped myself up in the blanket and slept.
I wound the scarf around my neck several times.
I wrapped the gift up in newspaper.
I wound tissue around my hand and wiped it.
Please wind the rope around the stick.

examples.ko: 아이가 담요를 둘둘 말고 앉아 있어요.
examples.en: The child is sitting wrapped up in a blanket.

explain: 길거나 넓은 것을 여러 번 감거나 마는 모양이고, '말다', '감다', '싸다'와 잘 같이 써요. '돌돌'은 더 작고 가벼운 느낌이고, '둘둘'은 더 크고 두툼한 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It describes wrapping or rolling something long or wide several times, and goes well with '말다', '감다' and '싸다'. '돌돌' feels smaller and lighter, while '둘둘' feels bigger and thicker.

examples.en: He slung his backpack over his shoulder and went to the mountain.
Please sling the bag over one shoulder.
My father shouldered a shovel and went out to the field.
Now that I've slung the load over my shoulder, it's heavier than I thought.
A student with a guitar slung over his shoulder walked by.
Why did you sling such a big backpack over your shoulder?

explain: '메다'를 조금 길게 한 말이라, 말할 때는 그냥 '메다'가 훨씬 자연스러워요. 가방, 배낭, 삽처럼 어깨 위로 올리는 물건과 써요. 손에 들 때는 '들다'를 써요.
explain_en: It is a slightly longer form of '메다', and in speech plain '메다' sounds far more natural. It goes with things you put over the shoulder, like bags, backpacks and shovels. When you hold something in your hand, use '들다'.

examples.en: People stood in a ring around the scene of the accident.

examples.ko: 아이들이 선생님 주위에 둘러서서 이야기를 들었어요.
examples.en: The kids stood around the teacher and listened to the story.
Everyone, please gather in a circle around the cake.

examples.ko: 구경꾼들이 길거리 공연 앞에 둘러서 있어요.
examples.en: Onlookers are standing in a circle in front of the street performance.
The people standing around clapped.

examples.ko: 그냥 둘러서 있지만 말고 좀 도와주세요.
examples.en: Don't just stand around, please help a little.

explain: 가운데에 있는 사람이나 물건을 향해 동그랗게 서는 모습을 말해요. 앉아서 그렇게 할 때는 '둘러앉다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It describes standing in a circle facing a person or thing in the middle. When people do the same while sitting, it is '둘러앉다'.

examples.en: We put a fence all around the field.
They have put up a tarp all around the construction site.

examples.ko: 마당에 담을 둘러치면 집이 더 안전해 보여요.
examples.en: If you put a wall around the yard, the house looks safer.

examples.ko: 텐트 주변에 줄을 둘러쳐서 들어오지 못하게 했어요.
examples.en: We strung a rope around the tent so no one could come in.
We received guests in a room surrounded by a folding screen.

examples.ko: 집 앞에 임시로 막을 둘러치는 중이에요.
examples.en: We are setting up a temporary screen around the front of the house.

explain: 울타리, 담, 병풍처럼 세우거나 걸어서 빙 둘러 막을 때 써요. '두르다'는 목도리처럼 몸에 감을 때도 써서 범위가 더 넓어요. 말로 하는 변명은 '둘러대다'라고 해요.
explain_en: Use it when you set up or hang something like a fence, wall or screen to enclose an area. '두르다' is broader and also covers things like wrapping a scarf around the body. For making an excuse in words, the verb is '둘러대다'.

examples.en: This bread is round and flat.
He has a round, broad face and looks friendly.
I put the fruit on a round, wide plate.
I picked up a round, flat stone at the stream.
Please spread the dough out round and flat.
The baby's hands are round and chubby, so they're cute.

explain: 동글면서 납작하고 넓은 모양에 써요. 돌, 접시, 빵 같은 물건에 많이 쓰고, 사람 얼굴에 쓸 때는 듣는 사람이 기분 나쁠 수 있어서 조심해요.
explain_en: It is used for shapes that are round and also flat and broad. It is common for things like stones, plates and bread; when used for a person's face, it can offend the listener, so be careful.

examples.en: There are many round, smooth stones by the river.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 성격이 둥글둥글해서 친구가 많아요.
examples.en: He has an easygoing personality, so he has many friends.
Please shape the dough into round balls.
The baby is round and cute-looking.
I made the snowman nice and round.

examples.ko: 할머니는 둥글둥글 큰 호박을 따 오셨어요.
examples.en: Grandma brought a big, round pumpkin she had picked.

explain: 모양이 모나지 않고 둥근 것뿐 아니라, 성격이 부드럽고 원만하다는 칭찬으로도 써요. 성격 이야기에서는 '둥글둥글하다'로 많이 말하고, 반대는 '모나다'예요.
explain_en: Besides round shapes without corners, it is also a compliment for a gentle, easygoing personality. For personality it is usually said as '둥글둥글하다', and the opposite is '모나다'.

examples.en: A cloud is floating in the sky.
The balloon floated away on the wind.
The moon rose softly over the mountain.

examples.ko: 물 위에 오리가 둥실 떠 있어요.
examples.en: A duck is floating on the water.
The boat sways gently on the river.
We floated and played in the sea on an inner tube.

explain: 가볍고 부드럽게 떠 있거나 떠오르는 모습이에요. '둥실둥실'이나 '두둥실'처럼 늘여서 쓰면 더 느긋하고 시적인 느낌이 나요.
explain_en: It describes floating or rising lightly and softly. Stretched forms like '둥실둥실' or '두둥실' sound more relaxed and poetic.

examples.en: There is a persimmon tree in the back of my grandmother's house.
We spread the peppers out to dry in the back yard.
The kids are playing hide-and-seek in the back yard.
If you go around to the back, you'll see a small vegetable garden.
The jar stand was usually at the back of the house.
I hung the blanket on the clothesline in the back yard.

explain: 집 뒤쪽의 마당이나 공간으로, 시골집이나 한옥 이야기에서 자주 나와요. 요즘 일상 대화에서는 '뒷마당'이 더 흔하고, 반대는 '앞마당'이에요.
explain_en: It means the yard or space behind a house, and often appears in stories about country homes or hanok. In everyday talk today '뒷마당' is more common, and the opposite is '앞마당'.

examples.en: I followed right behind the rear of the car ahead.
There is an ad on the back of the bus.
The puppy just trails along right behind its owner.
The tail end of the train got farther and farther away.

examples.ko: 저는 줄 맨 뒤꽁무니에 서 있었어요.
examples.en: I was standing at the very back of the line.
That kid tags along behind his older brother.

explain: '뒤'를 좀 더 생생하고 편하게 말하는 구어체예요. 차나 줄의 맨 끝에도 쓰고, 사람에게 '뒤꽁무니를 쫓아다니다'라고 하면 계속 졸졸 따라다닌다는 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It is a more vivid, casual way of saying '뒤' (back). It is used for the very end of a car or a line, and '뒤꽁무니를 쫓아다니다' for a person means tagging along behind someone all the time.

examples.en: The penguin waddles along.
The baby wobbled when first learning to walk.
I saw a duck waddling because it was so full.
My shoes are big, so I keep wobbling.
I have too much luggage, so it's dangerous if I wobble.
Don't wobble, try walking straight.

explain: 몸이 좌우로 기울며 흔들리는 걸음을 말해요. 오리, 펭귄, 아기처럼 통통하고 귀여운 대상에 잘 어울려요. '비틀거리다'는 힘이 없거나 아파서 쓰러질 듯한 느낌이 더 강해요.
explain_en: It describes a walk where the body tilts and sways from side to side. It suits chubby, cute subjects like ducks, penguins and babies. '비틀거리다' feels more like being weak or sick and about to fall.

examples.en: The duck waddles over.
The penguins waddle along in a line.
The child toddled over to her mom.
The bicycle wobbles, so I feel uneasy.

examples.ko: 큰 가방을 메고 뒤뚱뒤뚱 계단을 올랐어요.
examples.en: I climbed the stairs unsteadily with a big bag on my back.
It's a robot that moves with a wobble like a teddy bear.

explain: '뒤뚱거리다'와 같은 느낌의 부사로, 몸이 좌우로 흔들리며 걷는 모습을 보여 줘요. 아기가 귀엽게 걷는 모습은 '아장아장'이라고도 하는데, '뒤뚱뒤뚱'은 몸이 흔들리는 것이 더 강조돼요.
explain_en: It is the adverb with the same feel as '뒤뚱거리다' and shows a body swaying from side to side while walking. A baby's cute steps can also be '아장아장', but '뒤뚱뒤뚱' stresses the swaying body more.

examples.en: My face is a mess of tears and sweat.

examples.ko: 서류가 뒤범벅이라 필요한 걸 못 찾겠어요.
examples.en: The papers are all jumbled together, so I can't find what I need.
My whole body got covered in mud.
It was a day when joy and sadness were all mixed together.

examples.ko: 책상 위가 뒤범벅이니까 정리 좀 하세요.
examples.en: Your desk is a total mess, so please tidy it up.
The child came running, smeared all over with paint.

explain: 여러 가지가 마구 섞여 지저분하거나 복잡한 상태예요. 'A와 B 뒤범벅', '~으로 뒤범벅이 되다'처럼 써요. '뒤죽박죽'은 순서나 차례가 엉킨 느낌이 더 강해요.
explain_en: It is a state where many things are mixed together messily or confusingly. It is used like 'A와 B 뒤범벅' or '~으로 뒤범벅이 되다'. '뒤죽박죽' feels more like order or sequence being tangled up.

examples.en: The road got covered in mud because of the rain.

examples.ko: 여러 소리가 뒤범벅돼서 잘 안 들려요.
examples.en: Many sounds are mixed together, so I can't hear well.
Put the papers in a file so they don't get mixed up.
My feelings were all jumbled together and I couldn't speak.
My clothes ended up smeared all over with paint.

examples.ko: 기억이 뒤범벅되어 정확히 생각이 안 나요.
examples.en: My memories are muddled, so I can't recall exactly.

explain: '뒤범벅이 되다'와 같은 말인데 더 짧게 붙여서 써요. 지저분하게 묻거나 여러 가지가 섞인 상태 모두에 쓰고, 마음이나 기억처럼 눈에 안 보이는 것에도 쓸 수 있어요.
explain_en: It means the same as '뒤범벅이 되다' in a shorter, joined form. It covers both being smeared messily and having many things mixed up, and can also be used for unseen things like feelings or memories.

examples.en: Waiting for the exam results, my mind is unsettled.
Last night's dreams were disturbing, so I slept badly.
The mood at the company is unsettled these days.

examples.ko: 뒤숭숭한 소문 때문에 일이 손에 안 잡혀요.
examples.en: Because of the unsettling rumors, I can't focus on work.
When my mind is uneasy, I take a walk.
I ended up spending the day feeling unsettled.

explain: 마음이나 꿈, 분위기가 불안하고 어수선할 때 써요. '어수선하다'는 정리 안 된 방이나 분위기에도 쓰지만, '뒤숭숭하다'는 마음이 불안하고 안정이 안 되는 느낌이 중심이에요.
explain_en: Use it when a mind, a dream or an atmosphere feels uneasy and unsettled. '어수선하다' can also describe a messy room or scene, but '뒤숭숭하다' centers on the anxious, unstable feeling.

en: back way; back lane; back street

examples.ko: 그 가수는 이제 역사의 뒤안길로 사라졌어요.
examples.en: That singer has now faded into the backwaters of history.

examples.ko: 골목 뒤안길을 따라 걸으면 조용한 집이 나와요.
examples.en: If you walk along the back lane, you'll come to a quiet house.

examples.ko: 인기가 식은 뒤 그는 뒤안길에서 조용히 지냈어요.
examples.en: After his popularity faded, he lived quietly out of the spotlight.

examples.ko: 화려한 도시의 뒤안길에는 힘든 사람들도 있어요.
examples.en: In the back lanes of the glamorous city, there are people struggling too.

examples.ko: 그 기술은 뒤안길로 밀려난 지 오래예요.
examples.en: That technology was pushed aside long ago.
I found an old restaurant on a back street of the market.

explain: 원래는 집 뒤쪽이나 큰길에서 벗어난 길이지만, 요즘은 '화려한 모습 뒤의 잊힌 곳'이라는 비유로 더 많이 써요. 주로 글이나 뉴스, 이야기체에서 보여요.

phrases.example: 그 가게는 시대가 바뀌면서 역사의 뒤안길로 사라졌어요.
phrases.en: The shop faded into history as times changed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한때 있었지만 이제는 사람들에게 잊힌 것에 써요. 글이나 뉴스에서 자주 나오는 굳은 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for something that once existed but is now forgotten. It is a fixed expression often seen in writing and the news.

explain_en: It originally means the path behind a house or off the main road, but today it is more often used figuratively for the forgotten side behind a glamorous surface. You mostly see it in writing, news and storytelling.

examples.en: The earphone cord got tangled up inside my bag.
I heard the two cases are tangled up in a complicated way.
The story is so tangled that it's hard to understand.

examples.ko: 이해관계가 뒤얽힌 문제라 쉽게 해결이 안 돼요.
examples.en: It's a problem with tangled interests, so it isn't easily solved.
I cut off the tangled branches.

examples.ko: 기억과 꿈이 뒤얽혀서 구분이 안 돼요.
examples.en: Memories and dreams are mixed together and I can't tell them apart.

explain: '얽히다'에 '뒤-'가 붙어서 이리저리 심하게 엉킨 느낌이에요. 줄이나 가지뿐 아니라 사건, 감정, 관계처럼 복잡한 것에도 써요. 말할 때는 그냥 '얽히다'를 더 많이 써요.
explain_en: With '뒤-' added to '얽히다', it feels badly tangled in every direction. It is used not only for cords and branches but also for complicated things like events, feelings and relationships. In speech, plain '얽히다' is used more.

examples.en: Even if I rummage in my bag, the key doesn't turn up.
While waiting, I flipped through a magazine.
While rummaging through a drawer, I found an old photo.
I only leafed through the book and didn't read it.

examples.ko: 냉장고를 뒤적거리지 말고 필요한 걸 말하세요.
examples.en: Don't rummage in the fridge, just say what you need.
I searched my pocket for coins.

explain: 무언가를 찾으려고 이것저것 헤집거나, 책을 대충 넘겨 볼 때 써요. '뒤지다'보다 가볍고 느슨한 느낌이고, '뒤적이다'도 같은 뜻으로 써요.
explain_en: Use it when you poke around through things to find something, or leaf through a book loosely. It feels lighter and looser than '뒤지다', and '뒤적이다' means the same.
